result:
There is a small hour each morning when the city belongs to the people who keep it running but rarely appear in its stories.

A baker lifts the shutters with flour on her sleeve. A bus driver waits at a red light with no other cars in sight. Someone waters the plants outside a closed restaurant, careful not to splash the handwritten menu. In an apartment above a pharmacy, a child wakes early and watches the windows across the street brighten one by one.

Nothing remarkable happens. The bus turns the corner. The baker sets out yesterday’s bread at half price. The child goes back to sleep.

But by the time the rest of the city calls itself awake, a thousand small things have already been done on its behalf.
